raw.cause: nav handles display's MSG_ROUTE by doing MsgSend(MSG_POSITION) to gps and stays REPLY-blocked on gps. Under the deadlock fault, gps_handle answers that message by doing its own MsgSend(MSG_HINT) back to nav. nav is single-threaded and stuck inside MsgSend, so it never gets to MsgReceive. gps is therefore SEND-blocked on nav and nav is REPLY-blocked on gps. Neither side can ever reply, and display waits behind nav forever. The gps -> nav send also breaks the contract, which only allows nav -> gps.
raw.qnx_call: MsgSend in gps (gps_handle sends MSG_HINT to nav while nav is blocked in MsgSend to gps)
raw.fix_summary: Remove the gps -> nav send. Messages must only flow in the allowed direction nav -> gps, so a server must never MsgSend to one of its own clients. If gps really needs a route hint, nav should put it in the MSG_POSITION request, or nav should push it to gps ahead of time. Do not add a gps -> nav rule to blueprint.yaml: that would make the cycle legal.
